routes.name: Temporary Resident Permit for Employment (main applicant, off island)
Temporary Resident Permit for Employment (main applicant, in country)
Temporary Resident Permit for conduct of business (main applicant, off island)

note: Samoa, read on the Ministry of the Prime Minister and Cabinet's Immigration division pages (mpmc.gov.ws: its fees page and its Permit Services page) on 2026-10-30; fees are in tala. Temporary residence is issued for business and investment, employment, study, research, cultural or religious purposes and family. The Temporary Resident Permit for Employment is asked on the temporary residence form with an Employer Sponsorship form, medical and police reports and qualifications (the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour recommends whether employing a non-citizen is in Samoa's interest); 'the holder is permitted to work for the employer nominated in the application' (work for the sponsor), the permit being liable to cancellation if that employment ends. Its fee is SAT$900 for a main applicant applying off island and SAT$1,800 in country (written as two routes of one permit, abroad and in country), processing 10 working days. The business permit (conduct of business, on an Investment Certificate, a business licence and company registration) costs the same: SAT$900 off island (written) or SAT$1,800 in country; what work it allows isn't stated. Permanent residence costs SAT$3,200 for an adult, processing 10 working days; its conditions and years aren't on these pages. Holders of visitor, research and cultural or religious permits may not work. No permit's term or renewal is stated (an emergency renewal endorsement costs SAT$60). Naturalisation isn't read here.

sources.title: Ministry of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, Permit Services
sources.said: By legislation, we service four types of entry permits: Visitor, Temporary Resident, Permanent Resident, and Ministerial. ... Attach a completed Employer Sponsorship form ... Where a Temporary Resident Permit for Employment Purposes is granted, the holder is permitted to work for the employer nominated in the application. ... Visitors, Academic Researchers, Cultural and Religious personnel permit holders are not permitted to work in Samoa.
